title: The car swept off a flooded bridge on the way to a dance
summary: Buddy Bo's car was swept into floodwater at the Jordan River; the band was rescued by a truck and played the dance soaking wet.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: So, uh, I came over this Saturday evening and I...as he suggested that I do. And, uh, we got all the band together, which Ogis was a member at the time, Ogis' associate, with his bass. And after all the members of the band, we booted the car and we hated it for the kill. When we got out to Pearl River, not Pearl River, Jordan River, there were cars lined up, oh, two or three blocks on this side of the river and likewise on the other side. People have been tired of there for as much as 10 and 12 hours waiting for the water to go down. So we bypassed the cars because they walked on the right-hand side of the road and got to the bridge. The water was right up to the bridge, I said, just like that. It went over the bridge and further down, the embankment was built up and the water had covered. So, one fellow says, told Buddy, I think you can make it because your car is built kind of high. Well, my mind had led me to get out then, but I didn't want to be chicken, you know what I'm saying? I said, I go along with the deal. Bright moonlight night, just as we had nine. So, we starts off in the water. Now, mind I'll tell you, the incline was built up because of the swampy area. We get to about our .

half a block or so out and the current from that water rushing down from higher land. You can see those trees doing this, you know, waiting. Later on we heard the motor sputter and all of a sudden the water pushed the car clean off that embankment down into that deep water. And when that cold water hit my feet, unbeknownst to myself, I beat everybody out the car. I said, no, the top of it tilted. And I heard him say, wait a minute, wait a minute. I went out there. And under the water, if I was to say. And the drummer was John, what was his name? John what? John Cooks. John Cooks. He was out there in the water up the air trying to grab his ground sticks.
Yeah? Boy, we could have all gotten drowned.
So much for that. All this was gotten ruined then. Yeah. So we got out and we sat on. Interesting, Jim.

We sat on the top of the car when someone over on the other side saw when the car went down. So they sent a big heavy truck, Landon's Frederick, the man we were playing for. He sent a truck out there. And I think three or four white boys came out on that truck. And saved us, you might as well put it to that. They did save us because we were marooned there, we couldn't move. So that big heavy truck, the current couldn't push it as they bought an ordinary automobile. So they picked us up. We got on the truck with the instruments. Went to the poor, uh, Jersey Riverside, turned around and went back. So when we got there, Leonard told Buddy, he said, Buddy, I told you the dance was off. Oh, Buddy said, well, you know, you said, we said every Saturday night, so he held his feet to the fire today, he said, however, we played. When the dance was over, Leonard explained to Buddy, he said, now Buddy, you know, I asked you not to come. He said, but I'm going to ask you to cut a dollar off each man, because you see I didn't make anything. Well, oh no, I want my money, I'll get you my money. So he paid him his money. Now we didn't have automobile one to get back. Oh. So after he paid him, now that would have been, there was only six of us, six dollars a cut would have been. So after we finished playing, Buddy talked about how about getting back on him, the man said, nothing done. He said, that's your hard luck. So now we had the hire man a dollar piece, anyhow. Right on. And he had an old regular truck.

We broke down about four times. He had to stop and pick the truck on the way. And incidentally when we passed by the section where our car was, we seen where the water had been trying to clean upside down. The car was right. It was no more good for anything else. Now this is one thing I want to ask you.
Y'all must have, y'all sit down and play all soaking wet and everything?
That's right. Soaking wet. The instruments always.
That music must have sounded some good.
